paragraphs.source_en: Exhibit 7.1 shows that $10,000 invested in a low-cost S&P 500 index fund in 1991 earned a nominal (before-inflation) profit of $77,000. The average equity fund earned a profit of just $55,500—72 percent of what was there for the taking. The compound return earned by the average fund investor tumbled to $36,100, less than 50 percent of the $73,100 return earned by investors in the simple index fund. These penalties add up!

paragraphs.source_en: While the data clearly indicate that fund investor returns fell well short of fund returns, there is no way to be precise about the exact shortfall.2 But the point of this examination of the returns earned by the stock market, the average fund, and the average fund owner is designed not for *precision*, but for *direction*.
